articles.title: Clock Tower - Finding the Zealot and Defeating Dracula Walkthrough - Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This is a continuation of IGN's walkthrough for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. For this section, we'll be climbing to the top of the Clock Tower
articles.body:
This is a continuation of IGN's walkthrough for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse . For this section, we'll be climbing to the top of the Clock Tower to face off against Isaac, also known as the Zealot. Isaac is one of the last bosses in the game you should face off against before confronting Dracula. However, before reaching this point, make sure to defeat the Shadow in Notre-Dame before reaching this point, as it gives you the bad ending. However, this won't end or stop your playthrough if you do. You can follow along with this playthrough to review the previous sections here .

Where to Find the Zealot in the Clock Tower

You can find Isaac in the final section of the Clock Tower, beyond the Upper Gallery and The Way of the Fist. Again, make sure you've defeated the Shadow in Notre-Dame before reaching this point. Additionally, if you're trying to unlock the true ending for Belmont's Curse, make sure to defeat the Miser , unlock the Judge, Sage, and the Temptress , and complete the Room of the Four Virtues in Notre-Dame . This gives you the Absolution Spell that you can use against Dracula.

You should be able to reach the Clock Tower Bridge without any issue. When you get here, Leon will warn you that if you do not feel ready, turning back is always an option. If you're ready to proceed forward, equip Death's Arcana, Soul Harvest, and interact with the Clock Tower.

Interacting with it with Soul Harvest removes the spell from the tower, allowing you to proceed forward without any issues to the glowing doorway to reach the Clock Keeper's Atrium. (If you want to see the bad ending, interact with the Clock Tower again to reactivate the curse, and you can see how this plays out).

On the first floor, make your way to the left and you'll find that there are a handful of spinning blades. You can go past the first one, but the one preventing you from going upstairs will be moving too quickly. Head all the way across the gears to the left, and you'll find a spinning clock that you can hit. Interact with it once, and you'll slow down time around you, decreasing the speed of the moving blade.

Head back across the gears, and ascend to the floor above. If you miss the timer, return to the clock to hit it and try again.

Follow the pathway up to the top, and head through to the left side. You can use the purple anchor to help reach the platform, and then take the yellow anchor to swing through the spiked passageway, using your double jump and dash to make it to the top.

You'll enter a room with a massive clock wheel with a pair of spinning blades rotating around. Proceed to the right side, and there will be another interactable clock for you to slow down time.

You'll then need to head back to the clock room and use the purple anchor to reach the middle, but you'll need to remain in this section for a bit as the blades spin around. Wait until the pathway to the top is open, and proceed upward.

Head to the right, using your dash to slide through the spinning blades and then a jump to get over the last one. You'll land on the other side, to the right of the clock that you just used. Hit the lever, and you'll drop down, unlocking the blocked doorway that was next to the clock. Head through the glowing doorway on your right to go into the Bridge of Haste.

However, when you enter the location, there will be a spinning blade blocking your path that's moving too quickly. You'll need to return to the previous area, the Clock Keeper's Atrium, hit the clock close to the door, and then return to the Bridge of Haste to go along the gears. The blades are moving too quickly for you to proceed here effectively.

Take the path forward, avoiding the blades as you move across the gears. When you reach the center, jump onto the platform above you, and you'll find another clock.

Hit it when the first one's slowing effect runs out, and then proceed down the right path to avoid the moving blades. You'll be safe when you enter the final section of this hallway, with the knight with a shield, arrow archers, and skull spider roaming around. Defeat them if you'd like, and head through the right glowing door. This brings you to the Eastern Summit.

In the Eastern Summit, you can follow the path to the right to remain on course. There's a knight with a shield partially blocking your path halfway through, but you can ignore them if you prefer. When you reach the far right side, before heading upward, go through the glowing door to make your way to a Mirror of Life.

However, through the glowing doorway, there's an enemy ambush you have to take care of, with knights with hand axes, skeleton archers, and a werewolf that shows up before you can head all the way over to the Mirror of Life. Once you have the Mirror of Life, return back to the Eastern Summit and take the upward path.

Before you start your upward path, hit the clock on the left, and then head up. Instead of dealing with spinning blades, there are smashing fists, similar to the ones you found closer to the Builder, Talos. You'll need to use the small alcoves along the wall to protect yourself, waiting for the fist to slam down before heading up, and then making your way to the left side.

After you clear the fists, you'll enter a room with multiple skeleton archers and a knight with a shield. You can make short work of them before heading to the top of this section, where you'll find another slowing clock.

Hit the slowing clock, drop down, and proceed to the left, dodging the pair of smashing fists on the left path. There will be a glowing door on your left side to enter The Gauntlet, but make sure to drop down from this section here to open the path to make this part easier if you have to do any backtracking.

Inside The Gauntlet, you'll have a group of enemies ready to greet you. There's going to be a flying knight with a lance, a knight with a shield, and a pair of skeletons that shoot lightning. Take care of them first before heading down the lower left pathway. At the end of this hallway, you'll find a slowing clock.

Hit it, make your way back to the entrance, and then take the first platform up to your left and follow this path, heading upward. You'll scale a narrow passageway where a slamming fist is hammering down, and you have to avoid it to reach the top. At the top, slam downward and destroy the damaged floor to connect this path with the one below.

Here, you can interact with the slow clock, and then proceed back on the upward path to the left. There will be another set of slamming fists that you have to avoid, but you want to wait until you follow up the first one. If you can, dash through the middle section, and then head down. When you reach the bottom section, there will be a lever with a knight waiting for you. Take care of the knight, and hit the lever to reestablish another path to the slowing clock.

You can now use that slowing clock to proceed through the downward path to the left. Continue going to the left and wait for the fist to slam down. When it does, get on top of it, and then jump to the left as early as you can to avoid being crushed. You can then head through the glowing doorway, entering the Steps of Time.

Head up the stairs in the Steps of Time, and follow the path to your left. You'll enter a large chamber with multiple gears rotating on the bottom. Use them to jump up to the next platform, and you'll find a flying knight with a lance. Take them out, and then jump up onto the second rotating gears, followed by jumping onto the platform above them. There's another flying knight in this section as well. Proceed all the way to the top, and you'll find a slowing clock.

Although the path to Isaac, the Zealot, is on the right, take the pathway to the left. You'll unlock an elevator that takes you down to the Daedalus Crossing, and you can use that to connect to a second elevator that goes even further down to the Mechanic's Ascent and the Mirror of Life that's down there. Return back to this section, and head down to the right to find the boss door, leading you to Isaac.

As you go through the boss doors, you'll be greeted by Isaac. He's surprised that you were able to make it beyond the trap he has prepared. Still, he's more than ready for this opportunity.

A short conversation occurs between Rose and Isaac, where Isaac explains how he survived through the assistance of Death. Rose comments that he's stuck in his own personal hell, unable to see beyond Dracula's desire to use him. Regardless, Isaac is more than happy to finish what he started on the bridge in his real body this time.

As the battle begins, Isaac will be using much of the same moveset that he utilized when you first encountered his form on the Castle Drawbridge. One notable difference is how much damage his attacks do to you, so expect him to hit much harder. However, for the majority of this fight, he uses many of the same patterns and techniques you're already familiar with defending against.

Isaac consistently teleports around the arena. You have to worry about the platform you're standing on and the lower area underneath you. As he teleports, he'll attempt to close the distance and land heavy thrusts with his lance. These moves are telegraphed, and you should be able to parry, dodge out of the way, or completely avoid them, leaving him open to any attack you can use against him. He may perform one medium swing aimed at your legs or torso, or slash out with two strikes at you after he teleports.

Another repeated attack he may use is that he floats in the air and creates a pinwheel of projectiles using his staff. These projectiles originate from the center and gradually rotate out. You'll want to draw away from these attacks to create openings, making it easier to dodge them.

Isaac may also float in the air and release his lance, having it fly around the arena. It will be aimed in the direction it's going to rush toward. It's quick-moving, making it difficult to dodge, but you should have enough time to get out of the way and hit the exposed Isaac while he floats there.

A new attack that Isaac uses is a lance thrust. He winds up this attack on one side of the arena, and then rushes to your location. If he hits you with the lance, he deals a heavy amount of damage, pinning Rose, before tossing her, dealing even more damage. You want to avoid this attack whenever it comes up, either by double jumping in the air or ducking below and heading to the lower level. If you jump, though, there's a chance he might damage you as you hit his head, but it's not nearly as bad as being struck by the lance.

The last new attack that Isaac uses can happen on the upper or bottom platform. Here, he strikes the ground with his lance and creates a green clock emblem on the ground. The emblem explodes, creating lines of energy in a cross formation, depending on the location where Isaac is using this attack. This can be at the center, on the left, on the right, on the upper or lower platforms. This will hit multiple areas. You'll want to be at a cross angle from it, or jump over it when he fires it out. He does this three times, teleporting to new locations (usually) each time, or he remains in the same spot to fire them all out.

Those are the attack patterns that Isaac follows and unleashes against you during the first phase of his boss fight. After you get him down to zero, Isaac regains all of his health, and he a second phantom version of him appears in the arena.

The second phase of the fight doesn't change too much. Isaac still goes through the same attack pattern we've gone over. However, now the phantom version is also doing these attacks. The phantom Isaac might repeat the same attacks. It might attack you using Isaac's basic attacks or lance throws, while the original does the magic explosions. It might follow up with its own lance thrust attack after you've dodged the original's move.

Phantom Isaac is unpredictable, but you want to avoid it as much as you can. Although it's there, doing any damage to it does not hurt the original Isaac. Expect this process to happen four times, having to lower Isaac's full health down to zero four separate times before death finally takes him. Each time, the phantom version and original become increasingly faster and more aggressive. There's a brief animation between each phase, giving you time to heal if you need to take it.

After the fourth death, it will look like Isaac is attempting to pull himself back together. However, it won't take as long as it did the other times, and he'll explode, allowing you to add him to your Tarot card deck.

You'll unlock the spell Chronomantic Dive. With it, when Rose jumps into the air and falls down, she deals damage on the way down and creates a cross of green fire, damaging enemies along its path while also slowing them for a brief moment.

With Isaac added to your Tarot deck, he'll lament that he was unable to show Dracula what he was truly capable of doing. Rose will take pity on him, as she believes Dracula thinks little of Isaac and the others who follow him.

Before you proceed, there's also a weapon you can acquire on the ground: Isaac's lance. Pick it up, and you'll unlock Chauve-Souris, a legendary lance that you can add to your collection and use.

With this weapon added, head up to the top platform and proceed to the left. You'll now be able to head upwards out of the Clock Tower and arrive at your final destination: the Master's Quarters, where Dracula is waiting.

Continue your path to the left as you proceed upward through the Master's Quarters in the Master's Quarters Approach.

You won't face much opposition moving forward. As you reach the end of this section, there's a knight and a few flying knights blocking your path, but you can bypass them to proceed to the blocked wall. You'll need to use your double jump and dash to reach the top. Hit the lever to open the blocked doors, and head down to the left section, bringing you to the Sanctuary of Solitude.

You can continue making your way down to the left. As you do, you'll face off against a pair of werewolves and a golem.

You'll need to dispatch them before making your way to the left, where you'll find the Sanctuary of Solitude's Mirror of Life. You can save and make a checkpoint there, while also restoring your lost health.

Continue to the left, and make your way through the latter half of the Sanctuary of Solitude. You'll encounter an enemy ambush in this next room, and you'll have to fight through a large raven, several flying knights, the spheres with faces, elementals, and skeletons shooting lightning. Once they've been dealt with, continue to the left side of the room and head through the glowing doorway to the Grand Staircase.

As you ascend here, when you reach the end, Leon will ask you to stop. He'll briefly tell Rose that he can barely notice Dracula's Curse on her anymore, and that he feels that he's seeing the real her for the first time as they begin to end their journey. Here, Rose steels herself before entering the final room to face off against Dracula. Go through the glowing doorway, taking you to the Throne Room Antechamber, and you'll find the boss room doors for Dracula.

When you enter Dracula's chamber, a brief dialogue occurs between Dracula and Rose. Dracula welcomes the last Belmont who he believes will ever challenge him, as Rose promises that she is there to destroy him. Although he believes that Rose might know how to resist the night, the rest of humanity does not know this secret. And thus, he believes, they too will eventually go into the Night.

Dracula jumps from his throne, and the fight begins.

Dracula has a range of attacks that he's going to use against you. For this portion of the fight, expect Dracula to frequently teleport from left to right on the arena. After these teleports, he'll quickly unleash an attack, forcing you to refocus on different sides of the battle.

He has a basic slashing attack that he can hit you with when you're close by. It's a swipe that he does at his midsection, which can do a fair amount of damage to you. You can avoid it by dodging away or ducking down. He does other close-range melee attacks throughout this fight, such as a stomp that creates a small earthquake shatter in front of him.

Another melee attack that Dracula uses is a teleport and grab attack. Dracula will teleport to one side of you, be in the air, and attempt to slide forward, trying to grab you. If he succeeds, he pushes you into the ground before tossing you away. You can dodge this attack by going over it, or underneath it if you have enough time.

Dracula also uses multiple types of fire-based ranged attacks. The most common one is where he fires out a column of four fireballs. These can come in a combination of being on top of each other, but leaving you enough room to slide underneath them and too tall to jump over them, or being closer to the ground, giving you room to jump over them. Another is when he raises his hand to unleash a trail of fire to home in on your position. Finally, the third is when he draws his cape out and unleashes large molten fire rocks, sending several back-to-back at your location.

Another fire-based attack that he uses is a large column of fire. He unleashes it on a set location of the arena, and the fire column remains in that location for quite some time. You'll want to avoid that location, being on the right or left of it. If you touch it, you'll receive damage and a fire damage-over-time tick that you can heal with a health potion.

When you get halfway through Dracula's health, these attack patterns remain the same. However, the significant change is that he will summon three of the fire pillars that stand side-by-side with each other. He'll then teleport to your side and cycle through his available attacks, aggressively attempting to hit you with them.

One new attack that Dracula uses after he loses half of his health is that he summons a fire storm above your head. He calls this attack with a quick flair of magic in his hand, and storm clouds form above your head. As the storm clouds remain, several fireballs begin to rain down from above, and you'll have to dodge out of the way. Dracula is free to attack and move around during this, forcing you to focus on his regular attack pattern alongside this continual threat.

When Dracula does reach zero health, he looks defeated, and Rose approaches him saying how he's done. However, he uses this opportunity to grab her, informing her that while this body becomes dust, he is not ready to give up the night quite yet. With Rose in tow, he flies upward, taking you to the roof.

How to Defeat Dracula Beast Form (Second Phase)

There, Dracula reveals his true form. You'll then be battling against a much larger version of Dracula on his castle's roof, and he has a brand-new moveset you'll have to learn. This is Dracula's Beast Form, as he looks like a demonic bat.

Much like before, Dracula does teleport around the map. He's significantly faster in this form, and usually follows up this teleport with a three-hit combination, moving toward your location.

Another attack you'll have to look out for with Dracula is when he crouches down and begins to crawl toward you. This crawl is quick, and as he's slamming down with his claws, he does a small area-of-effect around them. You want to jump over this attack and dash out of the way of his path. He ends it with an uppercut in the air.

Dracula also teleports above your location before slamming down on the platform. Even though he might miss you, he always hits the platform, breaking it and decreasing the amount of space you have to move. You'll want to avoid this location, as you will fall. It won't kill you outright, but it does do a small bit of damage, and every bit of health matters in this final showdown.

Dracula may also fly on one side of the arena and slide to the other side. As he does this, he keeps one claw on the platform, raking it forward, hitting you for a significant amount of damage if you're in his path. Alternatively, he remains flying on this one side and fires out energy blasts at you. These blasts go out further than the halfway point of the arena and remain there. However, if you get close to hit them, they explode. You'll want to hit them at a distance and dash away to avoid taking any damage.

When you do at least 60% of his health, he'll be stunned for a short time and land on the platform. You can use this opportunity to get in some heavy hits, especially with your Arcana.

When Dracula gets to 60% to 50% of his health, he will teleport above you, summoning a massive rock. He brings the rock down onto the platform, breaking a significant chunk of it, leaving you little room to move around. You can try to place yourself on one side of the arena, rather than hitting the middle, as the middle leaves you as little room to move as possible. Dracula does not remain on this attack after he fires it down. He teleports to you and continues his attack pattern.

Dracula becomes much more aggressive at getting to 50% of his health. Expect his attack pattern to remain the same during this portion of the fight, but his attacks focus on destroying the arena to prevent you from having as much room to move around as you did previously.

When Dracula reaches zero, you'll have completed the battle and defeated the Lord of Darkness. However, this is the opportunity for you to get the Normal or True Ending. There are multiple requirements for the True Ending, whereas the Normal Ending only requires you to watch the final cutscene as Dracula unleashes his curse on Paris.

For the Normal Ending of Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, do not use the Absolution Arcana spell as Dracula is releasing his curse. Allow him to carry it out, and you'll get the Normal cutscene for the game. As the cutscene plays out, you'll see Dracula's Curse explode from his castle and radiate out all over Paris. Rose and Trevor will be watching from a distance as Dracula's Castle explodes, but the red clouds and dreary scene remain around Paris.

Rose comments that she believed she would never see this day. Although Trevor compliments Rose on having defeated Dracula, Rose warns that his curse remains. He has created the potential for him to return one day, and it's only a matter of time until he does.

You can get the True Ending in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse by using the Absolution spell as Dracula goes to release his curse. There are certain requirements you need to meet (which we outlined in the beginning, but want to readdress here):

Upon defeating Shadow Rose, you'll receive the Absolution Arcana and can face down Dracula. You do not need to unlock each of the Works of Mercy for this spell.

As Dracula is charging his curse, use the Absolution Spell, and it prevents it from being unleashed. The cutscene is similar in format to the Normal one, but the red clouds are not there, replaced by a bright, sunny day. Dracula's Castle is also not shown exploding, and is instead replaced by the return of the Notre-Dame structure.

Trevor and Rose's commentary is also the same, but Trevor notes that he believes they won't see the return of Dracula for a long, long time. Rose says that gives them plenty of time to teach humanity how to deal with Dracula, and eventually defeat him forever. Trevor also apologizes to Rose about her having to sacrifice her mother's cards to complete the Absolution spell. She's okay with it, as they taught her a valuable lesson that she hopes to share with others.

articles.title: Tech layoffs 2026: Tracking the job losses across Disney, Intel, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, Meta and others
articles.summary: There are only a few weeks left in the year and there have been more than 200,000 job losses across the tech industry. Here are the details.
articles.body:
2026 is almost over, but unfortunately we didn't get here without a ton of tech layoffs. In June, 14,000 job cuts happened at EV automaker Lucid, game developer Bungie, trading platform company Robinhood and others. Microsoft 's round of layoffs in July affected 4,800 jobs — mostly across its Xbox gaming division. Shortly after, companies including Samsung, Amazon, Uber and Monday.com followed suit.

According to many reports , the U.S. is at the center of these job cuts. Oracle has had the biggest impact on layoffs this year so far. The annual financial disclosure the company filed on June 23 showed the software giant cut 21,000 jobs over the past year, roughly 13% of its workforce.

"The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce," Oracle said in the filing.

In response to the numerous job cuts, California Governor Gavin Newsom in June unveiled a tool to track AI's impact on the workforce . "As AI advances, we aren't just watching from the sidelines; we're reimagining how we prepare California through strong governance and innovative policy." In addition, more than 4,500 Google workers signed a petition calling for layoff protections as things get worse. Some of the protections they're asking for include buyouts before mandatory layoffs and guaranteed severance.

TrueUp finds that layoffs seem to be moving at a faster rate than last year — over 245,000 workers in tech were let go in 2025, while there have been more than 200,000 layoffs in 2026 so far. Several of the companies below have laid off employees due to increased spending in AI. We'll get into the reasons for the layoffs.

Disney is reportedly planning to lay off thousands in an effort to cut annual costs by 20%. Layoffs have not been confirmed yet, but we'll update this story if and when they are. According to people familiar with the matter, the cost reductions could come from layoffs in addition to expense reductions.

Intel reportedly initiated another round of layoffs this month, primarily affecting its IT organization. The number of jobs affected this time hasn't been disclosed. This is just the latest in a number of layoffs at Intel in 2026 that, in total, have affected hundreds of employees.

Ubisoft's latest round of layoffs has reportedly affected 166 jobs, mostly in its Montreal and Quebec hubs. Ubisoft representatives told IGN that the job cuts were accounting for an "evolving portfolio and changing production needs."

Polymarket staff reportedly experienced layoffs, but the scope of which is not known. The reports also suggest the company has reduced the number of contractors it will work with moving forward, particularly in the marketing department.

Squarespace, the website-building company, is laying off 19% of its workforce, which amounts to about 300 people. "The changes are intended to simplify how we operate, sharpen our priorities and enable the company to move faster as we position Squarespace for its next phase of growth," Jeff Seedman, a representative from Squarespace, told TechCrunch. Squarespace's industry has been disrupted by AI, as "vibe-coding" website builders have become more popular.

Design software company Canva's recent layoffs will impact 22% of its staff, or just over 1,200 employees. According to reports , the company is reorganizing its business and merging its product, growth and platform teams. Canva is also looking to reduce "subspecialisation," which could result in remaining employees taking on more responsibilities.

Fintech company Block started its second round of layoffs recently, after cutting more than 4,000 jobs earlier this year. According to reports , the Jack Dorsey-led company hasn't disclosed how many jobs were affected this time around, but reportedly teams at Cash App and Square (both owned by Block) were affected.

Amazon reportedly laid off "fewer than 1,000 white-collar workers" in its stores division. That's the part of the company that oversees the tech giant's e-commerce website. Employees in the U.S., India and the United Kingdom were reportedly affected.

In an additional incident, Amazon laid off about 250 employees in its devices and services unit, according to a Reuters report . This comes after a number of new product announcements, including new Kindles and Echo devices . According to the report, the cuts mostly affect those in software development.

The cloud storage company Dropbox is laying off about 9% of its workforce, which accounts for roughly 200 employees. The job cuts primarily affect workers on the engineering, product, design, and G&A teams. "Today, we're making difficult choices about where we invest and how we organize Dropbox to achieve the product and growth priorities that will matter most for our long-term strategy," Dropbox co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi said in an email to staff. Alkarmi also announced that, alongside the layoffs, chief technology officer Ali Dasdan will step down.

While not officially new layoffs just yet, reports claim Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees. This is in an effort to further reduce costs in the wake of increased AI usage. According to the reports, Xbox, Windows, Copilot and finance divisions will be participating in the offer. Microsoft already laid off thousands of workers so far in 2026.

EBay will reportedly cut 9% of its workforce in an effort to streamline operations. The latest job cuts come after a previous round of layoffs back in February, which affected about 800 positions. "As we work to capture the significant opportunity ahead, this step was taken to ensure we continue to operate from a position of strength by aligning our teams and resources with our top strategic priorities," an eBay spokesperson said in a statement.

Vide game publisher EA will eliminate 400 jobs , or about 3% of its workforce. This includes shutting down BioWare , the development studio behind the Mass Effect games. The next Mass Effect title will be cancelled as a result of the layoffs. These job cuts come after EA told investors earlier this year that it would reduce research and development costs as part of a plan to save upwards of $700 million.

According to a report in The Wall Street Journal, Netflix will lay off about 1,000 people, which accounts for about 6% of its global workforce. The report says the bulk of the layoffs will affect Netflix's "product, tech, legal and human-resources teams." This latest round of layoffs is the biggest for the company since 2022, and it comes in the wake of Netflix struggling to increase customer engagement and overall growth.

A "large part" of the Airtable team was laid off on October 12. Federico Simionato, Airtable owner Bending Spoons' product leader, said on X that the layoffs were not due to the workers' abilities but rather the company's "deep belief that small teams ship more and better." The exact number of employees affected by the layoffs wasn't disclosed.

Workday will be laying off around 140 employees from the Bay Area, as part of an effort to trim its tech team. The cuts come as part of a broader plan to cut the company's global workforce by 2.5%.

Xbox announced it eliminated 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios and additional areas of the Xbox Game Studios division. These layoffs are part of a "reset" it announced this summer; the company already laid off 1,600 people in July, and said at the time that an additional 1,600 terminations were still to come.

According to a Bloomberg report , Apple has laid off an undisclosed number of employees from Fitness+, the company's exercise subscription service. According to the report, the layoffs affected those who worked in the audio side of the division, which includes features like Time to Walk and Time to Run guided audio workouts. Reportedly, offerings like this will be reduced — but not eliminated completely — from the service.

Oracle employees were impacted by yet another round of layoffs in September. The total number of employees laid off this time around is not currently known. The tech giant reportedly set employees early morning emails on Monday, September 14, letting those affected know it would be their last working day. It's also reported that, with these layoffs, Oracle is looking to offset the amount of money is pouring into AI chips and data centers. Earlier this year, Oracle laid off 21,000 people.

Uber announced it will cut 3,300 jobs, or about 10% of its workforce, in a big restructuring effort. "We are removing layers, simplifying team structures, refining our global location strategy, and focusing our people and investments against the biggest opportunities ahead of us," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement . While the cuts apply to both regular employees and managers, the company stated it will reduce the "number of employees who sit 7+ layers from the CEO" by 20%, and it will cut the number of "micro-teams" by almost 50%. The CEO's memo did not mention AI as catalyst for the layoffs, but it did explain that this restructuring will allow Uber to bring its services to more people, invest in more drivers and merchants and "build the autonomous future."

According to an AppleInsider report , Apple laid off at least 60 people in its Vision Group, which is the team responsible for the Vision Pro VR headset. A Bloomberg report notes that Apple is also laying off roles in its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which is partially responsible for some of the AI systems on Apple devices. Overall, its estimated the layoffs affect more than 200 people.

When it comes to Vision Group and Vision Pro, it's been reported that incoming CEO John Ternus would be putting that product category "on ice," so this seems like the start of that process. The Vision Pro headset came out in 2024 with an eye-watering $3,699 starting price, and it remains to be seen if Apple will be pulling out of the AR/VR category entirely in the future. The Intelligence Systems changes are reportedly tied to changes that are necessary for the technical architecture for Apple's newly AI-infused Siri.

The New York Times reported that TikTok will lay off 250 people and close its Nashville, Tennessee office in October. This location was home to, in part, some of TikTok's content moderation team, although the company has not specified the reason for the layoffs or which teams they primarily affect. "We have decided to close our Nashville office to streamline our operations and better align our teams for long-term growth," a press officer for what is known as the TikTok U.S.D.S. Joint Venture said in a statement to the Times.

Zillow will lay off just over 500 people as it enacts organizational changes across the company. "These are difficult decisions that reflect both the strides we're making in our strategy and the reality of what is required of us to grow at scale," CEO Jeremy Wacksman wrote in a press release . Wacksman didn't go into detail about what organizational changes were made, or which departments are bearing the brunt of the layoffs. "These changes are about ensuring we have a disciplined cost structure and getting more efficient, with the right people in the right positions," he wrote.

Etsy laid off about 220 people, or 12% of its workforce, as it attempts to simplify its organizational structure. The cuts primarily affected the product and engineering teams, and Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said that the layoffs were necessary to build "the organization we believe Etsy needs for the future." An Etsy spokesperson told CNBC that the cuts were not driven by artificial intelligence adoption.

Microsoft has begun another round of layoffs that affects 4,800 jobs , or around 2.1% of its workforce. The Xbox division is getting hit the hardest, with 3,200 roles getting cut through fiscal year 2027, Xbox chief Asha Sharma said in a post on X — 1,600 people were let go on July 6. Shortly after those layoffs were revealed, it was announced that Sharma was appointed to a U.S. Federal Reserve task force to help advise it on "productivity and jobs." Other appointees include Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz and Charles I. Jones, professor of economics at Stanford University.

Intel is reportedly downsizing its data center group, despite strong performance. The company hasn't disclosed how many roles would be affected.

Visa will be cutting about 2,600 jobs, which amounts to about 7% of its workforce. The layoffs will primarily affect the technology and product teams, and the impetus in part is to make the company more efficient. "To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney wrote in a memo. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa." But according to Bloomberg's report, AI was not the only factor to influence Visa's decision to do these layoffs. The company reportedly intends to reinvest in things like consumer payments and value-added services like stablecoin.

Software company Monday.com will be laying off 20% of its workforce, which comes out to about 630 people. This comes as the company makes a pivot to AI and is attempting to make its AI platform a core offering of its business. Earlier this year, it designed its main product around the idea that business customers increasingly want its employees to work with AI agents.

Patreon laid off 20% of its workforce, or 93 people, as a result of the company "changing our organizational structure and how we work." But Patreon was explicit in its email to creators and staff that "we are not making the above changes because we believe AI replaces humans." However, the email also said "AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry, though, including how we work."

Uber has reportedly laid off 10% of its customer service division, according to a Bloomberg report, as it looks to "embrace artificial intelligence" and simplify its ranks. The company also stated in May that it would slow hiring as it makes use of AI more internally.

Samsung is eliminating 179 jobs as it moves its New Jersey headquarters to Texas later this year. The move is expected to impact around 1,000 workers. We're now getting a fuller picture of what that looks like: according to Reuters , 739 roles at Samsung's New Jersey location have been affected in some way. Some have been offered relocation packages as the company shifts its headquarters to Texas, while others have been let go. In addition, it's reported that 100 roles in its Texas location, primarily in the mobile division, have also been let go.

Amazon will lay off some people in its artificial general intelligence group, although the company has not disclosed how many roles will be affected. "This is a fast-moving space, and we're sharpening our focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers, so we can move faster on what counts," an Amazon spokesperson told CNBC.

Sony Interactive Entertainment released a statement that it's cutting "a significant number of employees" from its Bungie workforce. That includes most of the Destiny team and some Marathon team members, as well as SIE teams that support Bungie's operations. The email didn't say how many employees were affected.

Electric vehicle maker Lucid announced it's cutting around 18% of its workforce, and also noted COO Marc Winterhoff's leaving the company, Reuters reported . The layoffs are in an effort to "​boost profitability amid growing competition." The cuts affect full-time employees, contractors and hourly manufacturing workers.

Cloud computing services company Rackspace laid off 750 workers , or around 15% of its workforce. The cuts are driven by a shift in focus toward AI.

EV company Rivian let go of hundreds of employees , which amounts to around 2% of the company's workforce, the Wall Street Journal reported . Those affected were part of Rivian's service and customer organization, which handled marketing and sales.

Trading platform company Robinhood is planning to lay off 10% of its staff to restructure, the Robinhood Comms account shared on X today — that's around 290 jobs. It's unclear if the layoffs are AI-related, but CEO Vlad Tenev noted the company will be "utilizing frontier technologies to push our execution even further."

Salesforce laid off at least 86 employees in California, though Business Insider sources say job cuts also occurred in Washington and outside the U.S. as well. The cuts reportedly affect employees involved with Salesforce's Agentforce AI product, Mulesoft IT integration tool and its Marketing Cloud software.

Groupon is planning to lay off roughly 25% of its workforce , which will result in 400 job cuts. Those positions are expected to be eliminated by the end of the third quarter. This is in an effort to restructure the company and rebuild it as an AI-native company.

In another set of AI-related layoffs, website builder Wix said it was cutting around 20% of staff. Wix cofounder and CEO Avishai Abrahami announced the cuts on X , pointing to the changes AI is bringing to the industry and stating "we need to become a faster, leaner, and flatter organization." He also put part of the blame on the Israeli Shekel to U.S. Dollar exchange rates, which impact the company because it's based in Israel. The cuts are expected to impact around 1,000 roles, based on Wix's headcount.

Webflow, a website builder and hosting company, conducted a round of layoffs that an employee called "a bloodbath" in a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle . It's unclear how many employees were impacted, but one anonymous developer from the company told the Chronicle they believe it was larger than Webflow's last major round of layoffs, which affected 8% of its workforce in 2024. As with other recent layoffs, it looks like a shift to AI is to blame here. "AI is rewriting the rules for how marketing teams create, test, and optimize digital experiences," CEO Linda Tong said in a statement . "And the companies that move decisively through moments like this are the ones that come out ahead."

ClickUp CEO Zeb Evans announced that the company cut 22% of its workforce as it turns toward AI to improve productivity. He claimed it "wasn't about cutting costs," but about funneling savings from the cuts "directly back into the people who stay." The company has introduced million-dollar salary bands reserved for employees who "create outsized impact using AI."

Intuit is planning to lay off 3,000 employees, or about 17% of its workforce, Reuters reports . CEO Sasan Goodarzi sent a memo to employees noting the layoffs would help the company's efforts of focusing on infusing AI across its services.

Meta has officially begun cutting 10% of its workforce , totaling around 8,000 employees. In addition, it plans to close 6,000 open roles. The reason is to allow more room for AI spending.

Like Microsoft, NPR is offering voluntary buyouts to 300 employees in the newsroom, but only 30 will be accepted. However, if the news organization doesn't receive its target number, it will result in targeted layoffs. The reason is due to the loss of federal funding.

The online retail giant cut more jobs this month, this time from the Selling Partner Services organization. These new layoffs come after Amazon cut roughly 30,000 jobs in rounds across October and January. A spokesperson told Business Insider that the most recent layoffs have affected a "small number" of employees. The Selling Partner Services team works with third-party merchants on Amazon, providing onboarding, logistics and account management support.

Cisco is cutting just under 4,000 jobs in Q4, CEO Chuck Robbins said in a blog post . Impacted employees will receive pro-rated payment of 2026 bonuses and will also receive "support in finding new opportunities" via Cisco's placement services. In June, it was confirmed that the layoffs include 471 workers in the Bay Area .

"While we are reducing roles in some areas, we are making clear, strategic investments — particularly in silicon, optics, security, and in our employees' use of AI across the company," Robbins said.

LinkedIn is planning to lay off 5% of its staff, which is around 875 employees, Reuters reports . An anonymous person told Reuters the reason is to reorganize teams and focus employees on areas ⁠where its business is growing. However, one of the sources said the reason was "not for artificial intelligence to replace jobs at LinkedIn."

GM is letting go of around 500 to 600 employees in the Information Technology sector, Bloomberg reports . The reason is to "trim costs and clear the way to bring in staff with skills in other technology areas."

Due to restructuring driven by AI, Cloudflare is cutting more than 1,100 employees . "Today's actions are not a cost-cutting exercise or an assessment of individuals' performance; They are about Cloudflare defining how a world-class, high-growth company operates and creates value in the agentic AI era," Prince and President Michelle Zatlyn said in an email to employees .

PayPal is planning to cut around 20% of its staff — nearly 4,800 employees — over the next few years, according to the Wall Street Journal . "First, we will remove duplication and layers from our organizational structure. Second, we will accelerate our AI adoption and automation across our operations," CEO Enrique Lores said to investors.

Cryptocurrency platform Coinbase is laying off 700 employees , which amounts to around 14% of its staff. CEO Brian Armstrong cites the current market and AI changing the way they work as reasons for the layoffs.

Microsoft is offering a first-ever buyout to up to 7% of its employees, CNBC reports . It's a one-time retirement program that's available for workers at the senior director level and below whose years of employment and age are 70 or higher.

Nike announced it's laying off 1,400 people this week. "Collectively, these changes will result in a reduction of approximately 1,400 roles in global operations, with the majority in technology," COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy said. "These reductions are very hard for the teammates directly affected and for the teams around them, too."

Amazon is planning to temporarily close a warehouse in Homestead, Florida, which will eliminate more than 600 jobs, Newsweek reports . The job cuts will start in July and continue through September but the giant company is giving employees the option to relocate to other facilities. The warehouse has only been open for just under two years but Amazon is already looking to update the site.

Battery recycling company Redwood Materials laid off 10% of its employees, totaling 135 people, TechCrunch reports . Those who were let go received an email from the chief HR officer telling them the layoffs were made "to sharpen our focus, our work and the size of our teams to support the direction Redwood is going in the future."

Snap is laying off 1,000 workers , which is 16% of its staff, Variety reports . The Snapchat parent company made the announcement just weeks after Irenic Capital Management asked the company to make changes to improve performance and revenue.

Snap is using AI to streamline operations and assist the now smaller workforce. "We have already witnessed small squads leveraging AI tools to drive meaningful progress across several important initiatives," Snap CEO Evan Spiegel said.

Just two months after taking over as CEO of Disney, Josh D'Amaro announced the company is laying off 1,000 of its employees, AP News reports . In addition, Marvel let 8% of its staff go after the call was made.

"Over the past several months, we have looked at ways in which we can streamline our operations in various parts of the company to ensure we deliver the world-class creativity and innovation our fans value and expect from Disney," D'Amaro said in a memo to employees. "Given the fast-moving pace of our industries, this requires us to constantly assess how to foster a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce to meet tomorrow's needs."

The wearable camera maker this year will eliminate 145 employees due to a restructuring plan to cut costs, the Wall Street Journal reported . The cuts are expected to last until the end of the year.

Vimeo is going through its third round of layoffs since it was acquired by Bending Spoons. This time, the company let go of more than 120 people, which is about 25% of its city staff .

It's been reported that 200 Meta employees in the Bay Area will lose their jobs at the end of May. That includes 124 employees in Burlingame and 74 in Sunnyvale. The company last laid off workers just a few weeks ago.

Oracle has begun implementing a big cull of its employee base . On the final day of March, more than a dozen Oracle employees announced on LinkedIn they had been let go from their jobs, Business Insider reports . It's unclear at this time how many workers were affected, but it was projected to be thousands at the start of this month.

Those laid off received the same email : "After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change."

The job cuts are reportedly to help Oracle stem a cash drain related its expenditures on AI infrastructure. In June, Oracle revealed that it had laid off 21,000 people as part of the cuts.

Deux Ex studio Eidos-Montréal announced on March 30 that it's laying off 124 people . In response, the studio head David Anfossi has decided to leave the company.

The cuts are a result of "changing project needs and impacts across production and support teams," the gaming company said in a LinkedIn post . It also noted that the decision to lay off these employees is not related to their talent or performance.

After already having layoffs in January , T-Mobile has cut even more of its workers, GeekWire reports . It's unclear how many people were laid off at this time, but it could be in the hundreds.

"To move even faster in a dynamic market while continuing to deliver best-in-class digital experiences for our customers, we're further aligning our IT organization to support future growth and innovation… This includes the difficult decision of eliminating some roles while continuing to invest and hire in areas," T-Mobile told GeekWire in a statement.

Meta began laying off hundreds of employees on March 25, totaling around 700 people, per The New York Times . Those impacted were part of the Reality Labs team, as well as social media and recruiting teams. Though still significant, this is a much smaller number compared to a Reuters report that suggested 20% off staff would be affected by layoffs due to the increased spending on AI.

This change comes as the company is shifting away from its metaverse creation, which includes Horizon Worlds for its Quest VR headset that's operated by the Reality Labs team.

The gaming giant on March 24 announced it was laying off more than 1,000 workers in an effort to right-size the staff of its popular free-to-play online shooter, Fortnite. CEO Tim Sweeney sent a note to his staff, citing the reason for the layoffs is due to the "downturn in Fortnite engagement," which means "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded." He made it a point to note the layoffs are not related to AI.

105 employees from the Red Storm Entertainment team were laid off by Ubisoft in an effort to cut costs, IGN reports . Game development has ended at the studio, so the downsizing will remain permanent. The company employed 180 people in 2022 but has seen multiple layoffs over the years.

Roughly 1,600 employees were laid off at Atlassian on March 16, which is around 10% of total workers. Ahead of the layoffs, Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes shared a message with the entire team, letting them know the reason is to "self-fund further investment in AI and enterprise sales, while strengthening our financial profile. We're also changing the way we work and reorganising around our System of Work to move faster." Impacted employees received an email shortly after this message went out.

articles.title: Every Team We'll See in Avengers: Doomsday
articles.summary: How many super teams will be in Avengers: Doomsday? A lot...
articles.body:
With the new “final” Avengers: Doomsday trailer as well as the recent reveal from Marvel of who exactly makes up Sam Wilson’s Avengers team in the film , some of the more casual fans out there might think, “OK, you have a Captain America, an Asgardian, a bug guy, and a couple of others. That’s our new Avengers.” To which the less than casual, more, shall we say, ardent fans will scream, “BRUSH UP ON YOUR MCU, MAN!” Because you know what? Doomsday will definitely be featuring more than just a simple, single team of Earth’s Mightiest Heroes.

Yeah, we’ve got X-Men, we’ve got Fantastic Four, and we’ve got a whole lot more too. So let’s take a look at all the super teams that will show up in the new movie when it hits (that we know of so far, anyway)...

(Note: We of course don’t know every character who’ll pop up in Doomsday, or how the events of the film will play out, so there could be – and likely will be – some flux to these team line-ups as the story unfolds. Exciting!)

The MCU version of the Avengers haven’t actually had that many adventures when you think about it, at least not onscreen. The original team was formed in 2012’s titular team-up movie, and then they returned in Age of Ultron three years later. But by the end of that film, a new line-up was formed – with Vision, Scarlet Witch, Falcon and War Machine joining while Iron Man, Thor, Hulk and Hawkeye left (leaving just Captain America and Black Widow as the sole remaining OGs). And then the whole Sokovia Accords thing happened two movies after that, which sent all the heroes into disarray. By the time Avengers: Endgame rolled around, it kinda seemed like, well, everyone was an Avenger?

And that mindset could be continuing into Doomsday. Based on the end of Thunderbolts, the Avengers name is getting thrown around by a couple of different groups now. In that film’s post-credits scene , the new Sam Wilson-led Avengers team is mentioned… by the Thunderbolts, who are now also calling themselves the Avengers. “But we are the Avengers,” says Yelena Belova. “The government said so. How does Sam Wilson not understand that?” Bucky Barnes responds, “Well, he does have the shield.” Indeed, it’s as if the idea behind the Sokovia Accords is still lurking here – do the Avengers work for the government or are they an independent operation? Sounds like we’ll have both in Doomsday.

This lineup is also interesting in that it’s got a couple of members from the first two incarnations of the team in Thor (who apparently is back from outer space, where we last saw him in Thor: Love and Thunder) and Sam. And while Scott Lang has worked with the Avengers plenty, he was nevery officially a member before this – although his inclusion here makes a lot of sense considering his history with Sam. As for Joaquin Torres, he’s a newbie, having been Sam’s partner in Captain America: Brave New World, as is Shang-Chi (though we did see the latter hero catching up with some familiar faces in his debut film’s post-credits , namely Wong, Captain Marvel, and Bruce Banner).

If you saw Thunderbolts, you know that this team came about as a result of Julia Louis-Dreyfus’s Valentina Allegra de Fontaine recruiting various super-powered folks over the course of the past few Marvel Phases, only to then try to have them all kill each other at the start of that film. Instead, they teamed up and saved New York City by the time of the closing credits, and so de Fontaine seized the opportunity to grab the spotlight and announced that they’re the New Avengers. She also owns Avengers Tower now, so, you know, convenient.

But also revealed in the film’s post-credits scene is that the New Avengers are losing the public relations war that is going on between them and Sam’s Avengers. And Sam has even filed for copyright of the name “Avengers.” Meanwhile, Red Guardian proposes that the team call themselves the New Avengerz, with a “z”...

This is a team of mostly “punch and shoot” type heroes – only Ghost and Sentry have truly formidable powers. They’ll definitely need some help against Doctor Doom.

Newcomers to the big screen – well, this incarnation of them anyway – the Fantastic Four just showed up in the summer of 2025, and now we’re all expected to be excited to see them meet up with our favorite heroes from 18 years worth of MCU and another 18 years of X-Men movies? Just not happening, sorry.

That said, Reed Richards and the gang will apparently be uniquely placed to inform the Avengers and X-Men about who it is that they’re up against, since the trailers for Doomsday have made it clear that the FF and Doom have a history of some kind in the universe that they hail from. This was left open-ended in The Fantastic Four: First Steps. Additionally, that film ended with Doom visiting with Reed and Sue’s baby son Franklin , presumably with a plan to kidnap the child and utilize the child’s reality-shaping powers to his own end. We see in the “final” Doomsday trailer that the FF visit Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter in the past, so could they be there to warn the couple that their own son might be in danger too?

You just can’t keep a good X-Men team down! Well, until you finally reboot them once and for all, which is currently happening with the Jake Schreier-directed X-Men movie that’s already cast new actors to play the likes of Professor X, Cyclops, Jean Grey, Storm, and more. So the return of the late Patrick Stewart’s Xavier, James Marsden’s Cyclops, and the rest for Doomsday feels like a sort of bittersweet last stand, if you will, that will almost surely end with their destruction. Will it be worth it just to see them in their classic comics costumes? Yeah, probably.

Do these guys count as a team? Who’s to say! They are an organized group of super-types (albeit with tech-focused abilities for the most part), so we’re including them. You got a problem with that? Then take it to He Who Remains. (Actually, strike that last part.)

Will Robert Downey, Jr.’s Doom have a team in Doomsday? It seems safe to say yes, and we think we have an idea of who they may be, too. They’re freaking powerful, actually. We already noted that he apparently kidnapped Franklin Richards – a baby that literally brought his own mother back to life. Speaking of which… we recently saw Doctor Doom resurrect Wanda Maximoff from the dead . Coincidence? And then there’s Bruce Banner, who wasn’t literally dead, but maybe just feeling a wee bit dead inside after losing control of the Hulk for the umpteenth time in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Yeah, Doom has grabbed/recruited him too.

Doom will also have the mysterious Latverian Witches working for him, plus those nasty mutant-hunting robotic Sentinels. Oh, and he always has Doombots ready to go. Now that’s a team.

In addition to the teams that we’ll see in Doomsday, there are certainly some notable names who were not, strictly speaking, on any specific team last time we saw them. You’ve got guys like Steve Rogers, who based on the trailers at least is going to be a big part of the movie. Namor is swimming around out there somewhere. Shuri, who is now the Black Panther, is also in the trailers. Kate Bishop actress Hailee Steinfeld recently confirmed that she’ll be in the film too, which has fans wondering if the long-rumored Young Avengers will finally come to be in Doomsday too. And rumors peg Daredevil, Wolverine, and at least one Spider-Man as showing up as well – but we’ll have to wait until December 18 to see how true that is, and what else is in store for Marvel fans…

Talk to Scott Collura @scottcollura.bsky.social , or listen to his Star Trek podcast, Transporter Room 3 . Or do both!

articles.title: 'I Made the Deal' – President Trump Takes Credit for Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia, Posts Bizarre AI Image to Celebrate
articles.summary: Jensen Huang returned yesterday as CEO of Nvidia, with the company crediting "input from senior levels of the United States government." And, just in case that wasn't clear, Donald Trump has taken all the credit.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang returned yesterday as CEO of Nvidia , with the company crediting "input from senior levels of the United States government." And, just in case that wasn't clear, Donald Trump has taken all the credit.

Yesterday, in an interview with CNBC , President Trump told reporters that he convinced Nvidia's board to take Huang back, saying he "made the deal" and that he "gave them assurances, at least everything we knew" that the CEO's return wasn't a risk to national security.

Trump also took to social media to celebrate after the announcement, even posting a meme with Jensen Huang in Donald Trump's place after the assassination attempt in Pennsylvania, but instead of raising a fist in defiance, Huang is holding up a red bra.

While Trump seems happy that Huang has returned, the reinstated CEO now has to face both houses of Congress in hearings about Nvidia's compliance with export controls. Politicians from both parties are demanding answers about how many GPUs have been exported to embargoed countries like China and Russia.

Massachusetts Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren posted on X / Twitter: "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and Nvidia still owe Congress answers. The Trump Administration needs to explain what 'input' was given and by which senior officials to support Huang’s reinstatement."

What's more surprising is that Senator John Curtis, a Republican from Utah, echoed Warren's concerns, posting on X / Twitter: "Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?"

Despite these ongoing concerns, at least some Nvidia employees seem happy with Huang's return. An Nvidia employee posted a video on X / Twitter, below, of Huang getting a standing ovation in the lobby of the company's headquarters.

if you come for the king, you best not miss — abir (@aburducky) November 23, 2026

if you come for the king, you best not miss

It's unsurprising that Huang would be welcomed back in this way, after an internal movement among employees to reinstate the CEO picked up quite a bit of steam immediately after his resignation. But while there was a crowd of cheering employees, there are at least some employees who feel like his return is a mistake, with one engineer anonymously telling Yahoo Finance : "This is the worst outcome. We already paid the price of his departure but are still saddled with working for a jerk."

In the fallout of Huang's departure, reports emerged that painted a picture of his management style. For example, he allegedly told one employee that he'd "pee on [their] brain."

It's still early days for Huang's return to Nvidia, and with everything that's happened in the last two weeks, it's impossible to guess what's going to happen next. But now that his return has breathed new life into the AI market, it's unlikely that RAM prices are going to come down any time soon.

articles.title: Why Director Robert Eggers Calls His Brutal New Horror Movie Werwulf the Darkest Film He Has Ever Made
articles.summary: Werwulf just might be drector Robert Eggers’ darkest film yet. So bleak and dark, in fact, that Eggers recalled “when Jarin Blaschke, my cinematographer, first read the script, he said, ‘Does this take place in Hell?’”
articles.body:
“It was after Nosferatu and I said, ‘What's the darkest thing I can write?’” filmmaker Robert Eggers recently told me about the genesis of his upcoming horror film, Werwulf . The film takes place in 13th century England and follows a farmer, simply called Man, who has been cursed to live as a werewolf.

“Werewolves [in medieval European folklore] were doing things that were so extreme and taboo and violent that the culture couldn't accept that they were human and so they called them werewolves,” Eggers said about the historical underpinnings of his film. “So I thought that this was going to be the right so-called creature to inhabit a very dark movie.”

Werwulf just might be Eggers’ darkest film yet. So bleak and dark, in fact, that Eggers recalled “when Jarin Blaschke, my cinematographer, first read the script, he said, ‘Does this take place in Hell?’” Eggers and Blaschke’s collaboration goes all the way back to the helmer's feature film directorial debut, 2015’s The Witch. They’ve since worked together on each of Eggers’ subsequent pictures ( The Lighthouse , The Northman , Nosferatu , and now, Werwulf).

“When I did more research about werewolf folklore, it's very different from what we've seen in cinema. I understood that this also gave me the opportunity to explore some things that I explored in The Witch and – for reasons of my own inexperience and talent at the time and also for reasons of budgetary limitations – couldn't quite do, and I got a chance to try it again [in Werwulf],” Eggers said.

“I think I've derided The Witch on many occasions but I am proud of the screenplay and the screenplay was good. And as Alfred Hitchcock said, the three things you need to make a great film are script, script, script, so I think that, for the people who really relate to The Witch, I think that that is why. And then The Lighthouse, I love The Lighthouse but there's barely a story. And The Northman's Hamlet and Nosferatu was Dracula and this is finally an original story with a driving narrative again.”

In this exclusive clip from Werwulf, which can be viewed via the player above , Aaron Taylor-Johnson’s Man has been drafted by the King’s wolf hunters to join them in pursuing the wolves that are killing the sheep pivotal to England’s wool trade , the country’s biggest economy. While on the hunt, the man has an eerie encounter with a wolf where, for lack of a better phrase, game recognizes game.

“Aaron is the only person who could have played this role. I wrote the role for him. He's a very handsome man in a traditionally masculine way; he can grow a huge beard [and] he also has a haunted quality to him, but he also has a dance background. So I knew that he would be capable of this incredible movement,” Eggers said. “And it was one of the things that excited me the most about what the werewolf transformations would be in this film, is that it is physically the actor doing most of it. Yes, David White, the special effects makeup designer, does more stuff after that, but I wanted it to be grounded in this body that is in agony.”

Taylor-Johnson worked for months with choreographer Marie-Gabrielle Rotie to perfect the movements required to portray the terror and pain of the werewolf transformations. The actor also took it upon himself to study wolves.

“I gave him a tremendous amount of research that I thought would be helpful, but it was something that I wasn't proposing that he wanted to do, [which] was to go to a wolf sanctuary and hang out with some real wolves,” Eggers recalled.

“It was one of the best things we did in prep also because it was something that I wasn't thinking of and it changed the film. It changed his physicality [and] the way that the alpha male wolf interacted with Marie-Gabrielle - she was there as well - influenced how Aaron's character interacts with Lily Rose [Depp], who plays his wife, physically. And then also the howl of the alpha male wolf being so close to him was really mind-blowing because, obviously, you have the high pitch mournful howl, but when you're a bit closer you also feel this subwoofer reverberating in my ribcage, not just the wolf's ribcage. It was really quite amazing. It was intimidating.”

Look for my full on-camera interview with Robert Eggers closer to when Werwulf opens in theaters December 25. Tickets to see Werwulf in 35mm are now available .

articles.title: Over Half of GTA 6 Watch Time Came From Viewers Under 25 Years Old
articles.summary: The bulk of fans watching streams of GTA 6 are under 25 years old, according to recent stats compiled by StreamsCharts.
articles.body:
The bulk of fans watching streams of GTA 6 are under 25 years old, according to recent stats compiled by StreamsCharts.

After 13 long years, GTA 6 is finally out in the wild. Rockstar’s highly anticipated release has already broken numerous records, one of the most impressive being that it became the single most popular game ever on both Twitch and Kick just 26 hours after its global release.

Now that it’s had a little time to breathe, more data is rolling in, including information about who’s watching streamers play the game. StreamsCharts , a data analytics company that studies games-focused streaming platforms, discovered that most viewers of GTA 6 broadcasts tend to trend under the age of 25.

According to Streamlabs’ stats, 30.8% of viewers in GTA 6 streams are 20 - 24 years old, making up the bulk of those watching the game across Kick, Twitch, and YouTube. (Painfully, StreamsCharts pointed out that these players were in elementary school when GTA 5 came out.) 16.8% of these viewers are 17 - 19, with 8.5% accounting for viewers 16 or under. The second-largest age range watching GTA 6 streams are viewers aged 25–29. 11.6% of viewers are 30–34, and the numbers keep dropping from there.

StreamsCharts also found that an overwhelming majority of these viewers are single men, accounting for 83.8% of the gender divide. That’s not to say that gals aren’t also watching streamers play Rockstar’s latest; 14% of viewers are female, and if you’ve been on social media lately, you’ve probably seen a fair few female players showing off their outfits for Jason and Lucia or the viral conversation about how it’s, oddly, comparable to a crime-focused version of The Sims.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the United States makes up the bulk of GTA 6 viewership. Brazil isn’t far behind, coming in at 12.4% of the game’s total audience; Spain and Germany follow at 6.9% and 6.8%, respectively.

Certain games have also experienced a drop in viewership following GTA 6’s release. StreamsCharts found that GTA 5 had the sharpest drop-off on Twitch, followed by the platform’s Just Chatting category and World of Warcraft.

The GTA hype train is in full swing, and it’s making big bucks for Rockstar. The company reportedly made a staggering $3.79 billion from the game in just 24 hours, making it the single biggest entertainment launch in history. Internet provider Comcast even revealed that it experienced its highest-traffic day ever as players downloaded the game to their consoles, and PlayStation confirmed that GTA 6 was its biggest game launch in the company’s history.

articles.body:
The Spotted Seal is a secret mount you can get in Crimson Desert 's Charting the Unknown DLC. You can actually tame and ride the seals you find on Iliya Island, but there are a few hoops to jump through first. Here's how to find and tame a seal mount in Crimson Desert.

Spotted Seals can be found all along the beaches of Iliya Island east of the Great Coral Reef. They hang out in groups and spend most of their time sleeping.

You can only tame a Spotted Seal once it's in the water. Find a group of seals, then try to chase them into the sea.

It's finicky, but you can always go find another group of seals if they get away. Once you get a seal into the water, you'll see the prompt to hold Square / X to ride them like any other aquatic mount.

To keep a Spotted Seal permanently , open your inventory while mounted and then feed it food to raise its trust to 100. Then, you can take it in and register it as a mount!
